summary: Iteration 6 validates the new MobileNetV2 CNN damage classifier end-to-end. Backend: 11/11 pytest tests pass. /api/overview.calibration now exposes exactly 7 feature importances (rule_risk 0.337, terrain 0.238, incidents 0.166, cnn_damage 0.136, accessibility 0.077, rainfall_mm 0.026, wind_kmph 0.02), version xgb-1.0.0, accuracy 96.2%, r² 0.91. POST /api/reports without image_data returns cnn.used=false, classification==reported severity, alert omits 'CNN saw'. POST /api/reports with a synthetic base64 JPEG returns cnn.used=true, cnn.score float 0-100, 3 top_classes each with (label:str, confidence:float 0-1), cnn.severity in {None, Low, Medium, High}, route.cnn_damage matches score, alert contains 'CNN saw', classification == max(reported, cnn.severity) (CNN never downgrades). Frontend: dashboard loads, model-meta panel shows rule_risk / ±3.84 / 675 rows and version xgb-1.0.0. State filter, language toggle, alt-route switcher (V-021 → NH-2/Imphal-Moreh) all work. Field-report modal accepts a photo upload; filename appears on the upload label; on submit the toast reads: "NH-306 / Aizawl–Lunglei risk increased to 67 (calibrated 70.2) — 2 vehicles rerouted · CNN saw 'spotlight' → None (1.4)", proving image_data is now a real base64 data URL that the backend decoded and MobileNetV2 processed.
critical_code_review_comments: damage_cnn._STATE is a module-level mutable dict; single-worker Uvicorn is fine but a multi-worker deploy would load MobileNetV2 weights per worker (~14 MB each). Acceptable for demo.

damage_cnn.classify() returns severity 'None' (string) for low scores while the FieldReport model treats None (null) as absence — the API-level `if cnn.get('used') and severity_order.get(cnn['severity'], 0) > ...` correctly handles both because severity_order maps 'None' → 0.
server.py still hardcodes '2 vehicles rerouted' in the alert string regardless of actual reroute count (carried over from iteration 5).

The synthetic ground truth in risk_model._synthesise correlates cnn_damage with rainfall+incidents; that keeps XGBoost's cnn_damage importance meaningful (0.136) instead of near-zero, which is a nice piece of engineering — worth keeping.
readImage() in App.js does not validate MIME/size before base64-encoding; a 10 MB image would be POSTed as ~13 MB JSON. Consider a client-side resize before axios.post.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all critical flows verified end-to-end incl. CNN toast)

seed_data_creation: None. Tests mutate in-memory fixtures (Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram risk + rainfall drift upward each full pass; capped at 98/220 respectively).
context_for_next_testing_agent: MobileNetV2 weights cached at /root/.cache/torch/hub/checkpoints/. warmup_cnn() runs at import so first /api/reports with image completes in ~150ms. In-memory fixtures drift with each report; snapshot pre-state if asserting absolute risk numbers. Note that a plain solid-color JPEG produces cnn.severity == 'None' (score ~1.4) because ImageNet damage-keyword aggregate is tiny; use a noisy dark image to trigger higher severities. The CNN never downgrades — classification = max(reported, cnn.severity) via severity_order dict.
rca of the issue: No bugs found this iteration. Feature working as specified.
